advances: The proposed rank-linear bound for the original information content is false even under the mass guard for every proper real affine flat and an exactly integral original vector mean. The obstruction comes from a complete lattice polytope with three grid slices, each of codimension one. An exact temperature tilt balances slices of different cardinalities, while their intermediate lattice slice has exponentially smaller mass. No point or high-codimension flat has large mass. This disproves the information-content bridge, not the locked Weak Oertel conjecture, and makes no assertion about all-row likelihood prices or spatial lower-tail concentration.

proof:
First verify completeness directly. Let
\[
K_m=\operatorname{conv}\left(
  [0,2]^m\times\{-1\}\ \cup\ [1,5]^m\times\{1\}\right).
\]
For a fixed height \(t\in[-1,1]\), put \(\lambda=(t+1)/2\). A convex combination with that height has first coordinates in
\((1-\lambda)[0,2]^m+\lambda[1,5]^m=[\lambda,2+3\lambda]^m\).
Conversely every point of that box is such a convex combination: in each coordinate the weighted sum of the two intervals is exactly the indicated interval, and the same \(\lambda\) is used in all coordinates. Hence
\[
K_m=\left\{(\mathbf x,t):
 -1\le t\le1,\quad
 \frac{1+t}{2}\le x_i\le\frac{7+3t}{2}
 \text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
An integer point in \(K_m\) has height \(-1\), \(0\), or \(1\). The corresponding integer first-coordinate sets are exactly \(\{0,1,2\}^m\), \(\{1,2,3\}^m\), and \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}^m\). Thus \(K_m\cap\mathbb Z^{m+1}=D^{(m)}\). Both endpoint boxes are convex hulls of integer vertices belonging to \(D^{(m)}\). They therefore give \(K_m\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(D^{(m)})\), while \(D^{(m)}\subseteq K_m\) gives the reverse inclusion. This proves completeness.

For every \(i\le m\), the points \((\mathbf0_m,-1)\) and \((\mathbf e_i,-1)\) belong to the lower slice; their difference is \((\mathbf e_i,0)\). Also \((2\mathbf1_m,-1)\) and \((2\mathbf1_m,0)\) are supported, giving the difference \((\mathbf0_m,1)\). These differences generate \(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\). In particular the real affine rank is \(m+1\).

Write \(a_m=(m/2)\log(3/5)\) for the last coordinate of \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(m)}\), and let \(W_m=15^{m/2}\). These are local scalars, not aliases of any predecessor's apex probability or capacity conversion constant. The lower and upper slice partition sums are, respectively,
\[
3^m e^{-a_m}=3^m(5/3)^{m/2}=W_m,
\qquad
5^m e^{a_m}=5^m(3/5)^{m/2}=W_m.
\]
The middle partition sum is \(3^m\). Their sum is the displayed \(Z_m\), so the displayed probability table is exactly normalized. In particular it is strictly positive on the whole complete support and has one global affine logarithm. Since \(3^m/W_m=(3/5)^{m/2}<1\), both endpoint slice masses are \(W_m/Z_m<1/2\), and the middle slice mass is \(3^m/Z_m<1/3<1/2\).

Let \((\mathbf X',T)\sim p^{(m)}\). Its slice probabilities are \(W_m/Z_m\), \(3^m/Z_m\), and \(W_m/Z_m\) in height order. Conditional on each height, the first coordinates are independent and uniform on that slice's coordinate set. Their coordinate means are \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\), respectively. Therefore
\[
\mathbb E T=\frac{-W_m+W_m}{Z_m}=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E X'_i=\frac{W_m+2\cdot3^m+3W_m}{Z_m}=2
\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
This is an exact full vector mean, not a single directional mean equation. The point \((2\mathbf1_m,0)\) lies in the middle slice. It is also interior to \(K_m\), since its height and every first coordinate satisfy the displayed inequalities strictly.

We next prove the all-flat mass certificate. For a Cartesian grid \(B=B_1\times\cdots\times B_m\) with \(|B_i|=q\), and any real affine flat \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) of dimension \(r\), one has \(|B\cap G|\le q^r\). Indeed, the coordinate linear functionals restricted to the direction space of \(G\) span its dual. Choose \(r\) linearly independent restrictions. Projection onto those \(r\) coordinates is injective on \(G\): the difference of two points with the same selected coordinates belongs to that direction space and is annihilated by a basis of its dual, so is zero. There are at most \(q^r\) coordinate tuples in the grid. This includes \(r=0\), where at most one grid point can occur; an empty grid intersection contributes zero. Thus a uniform law on the grid gives \(G\) mass at most \(q^{r-m}\).

Fix any proper affine flat \(F\subset\mathbb R^{m+1}\) of dimension \(d\), and set \(k=m+1-d\ge1\). If height is constant on \(F\), its intersection with the support is empty unless this constant is one of the three supported heights. At such a height, its first-coordinate projection is a dimension-\(d\) affine flat. The conditional grid has \(q\in\{3,5\}\) choices in each coordinate, so the preceding count gives
\[
p^{(m)}(F)\le \Pr(T=t)q^{d-m}
=\Pr(T=t)q^{1-k}
<\frac12\,3^{1-k}\le2^{-k}.
\]
The inequality uses \(k\ge1\), \(q\ge3\), and the already established \(\Pr(T=t)<1/2\). It includes a singleton flat, for which \(d=0\) and \(k=m+1\).

If height is nonconstant on \(F\), then \(d\ge1\), and its intersection with each fixed-height hyperplane is a dimension-\(d-1\) affine flat. The first-coordinate projection preserves that dimension. Applying the same grid count at each of the three heights gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p^{(m)}(F)
&\le\sum_{t\in\{-1,0,1\}}\Pr(T=t)q_t^{d-1-m}\\
&=\sum_{t\in\{-1,0,1\}}\Pr(T=t)q_t^{-k}
\le3^{-k}
<2^{-k},
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(q_{-1}=q_0=3\) and \(q_1=5\). These two cases exhaust all real affine flats. The bound is proved by exact dimension and point counting; it does not depend on coordinate alignment of \(F\).

The original log probability is \(a_m T-\log Z_m\). The mean of \(T\) is zero, and its second moment is \(2W_m/Z_m\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{p^{(m)}}[\log p^{(m)}_{\mathbf X}]
=a_m^2\operatorname{Var}(T)
=\frac{m^2}{4}\left(\log\frac53\right)^2
  \frac{2W_m}{2W_m+3^m}.
\]
The covariance expression in the statement is the same identity: the first \(m\) tilt coordinates vanish and the last is \(a_m\). Now \(3^m/W_m=(3/5)^{m/2}\to0\). Consequently
\[
\frac{1}{m+1}\operatorname{Var}_{p^{(m)}}[\log p^{(m)}_{\mathbf X}]
=\frac{m^2}{4(m+1)}\left(\log\frac53\right)^2
 \frac{1}{1+\tfrac12(3/5)^{m/2}}
\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
For every proposed finite absolute \(A\), a sufficiently large integer \(m\) gives a strict violation of \(An\), with all hypotheses verified exactly above.

For the atomic claims, the uniform conditional lower-slice atoms have mass \(W_m/(3^mZ_m)\). The middle-slice atoms have mass \(1/Z_m\), which is smaller because \(W_m>3^m\). The uniform conditional upper-slice atoms have mass \(W_m/(5^mZ_m)\), also smaller. Thus \(p^{(m)}_{\max}=W_m/(3^mZ_m)\), giving exactly the displayed formula for \(\rho_m\). For \(s=3,4\), each atom satisfies \((p^{(m)}_{\mathbf x})^s\le(p^{(m)}_{\max})^{s-1}p^{(m)}_{\mathbf x}\). Summing and multiplying by \(2^{(s-1)(m+1)}\) gives the respective bounds \(\rho_m^2\) and \(\rho_m^3\), both tending to zero. These calculations remain atomic estimates and do not replace a computation of any depth moment.

Finally verify the entropy-row aliases, independently of the variance calculation. Every probability law \(\mu\) on \(D^{(m)}\) with mean \(\mathbf j^{(m)}\) has \(\mathbb E_\mu T=0\), so \(\mathbb E_\mu\log p^{(m)}=-\log Z_m\). Thus its relative entropy is
\[
D(\mu\|p^{(m)})=\log Z_m-H(\mu),
\qquad
H(p^{(m)})=\log Z_m.
\]
Nonnegativity of relative entropy, with equality only at \(\mu=p^{(m)}\), proves that the original \(p^{(m)}\) is the unique maximum-entropy row at its own integral mean. It is also the relative-entropy minimizer there, with minimum zero. The boundary-inclusive entropy-capacity identity of `bf1ff94487296374` gives \(\mathsf C_{p^{(m)}}(\mathbf j^{(m)})=1\). Under the exact likelihood normalization of `3e1cc0fa666b159b`, the log ratio of this row to its original source is identically zero, so \(V_{p^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}=0\). In contrast, its original log probability varies by \(2|a_m|\) between the balanced endpoint slices, and the calculation above gives its quadratic self-varentropy. No capacity weighting or continuous interpolation was used.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For every integer \(m\ge1\), set \(n=m+1\) and define the following new support in \(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb Z\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
D^{(m)}={}&\bigl(\{0,1,2\}^m\times\{-1\}\bigr)
\cup\bigl(\{1,2,3\}^m\times\{0\}\bigr)
\cup\bigl(\{1,2,3,4,5\}^m\times\{1\}\bigr),\\
\boldsymbol\theta^{(m)}={}&\left(\mathbf0_m,\frac m2\log\frac35\right),
\qquad
Z_m=2\,15^{m/2}+3^m,\\
p^{(m)}_{(\mathbf x,t)}={}&
\frac{\exp(\boldsymbol\theta^{(m)}\cdot(\mathbf x,t))}{Z_m}
\quad\bigl((\mathbf x,t)\in D^{(m)}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
The symbol \(D^{(m)}\) denotes this new support, rather than the Boolean-apex support \(D_n\) of accepted fact `3e1cc0fa666b159b`. The original source throughout this packet is \(p^{(m)}\); there is no reweighting of its roots.

This support is finite, complete, and full-rank, with saturated difference lattice:
\[
D^{(m)}=\operatorname{conv}(D^{(m)})\cap\mathbb Z^{m+1},
\qquad
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}(D^{(m)}-D^{(m)})=\mathbb Z^{m+1}.
\]
The source is strictly positive and globally log-affine. Its original vector mean is exactly the supported integer point \(\mathbf j^{(m)}=(2\mathbf1_m,0)\). For every proper nonempty real affine flat \(F\subset\mathbb R^{m+1}\), writing \(k=\operatorname{codim}F\), it satisfies the stronger coefficient-one bound
\[
p^{(m)}(F)<2^{-k}<2\,2^{-\operatorname{codim}F}.
\]
An empty flat, if included in the convention, has mass zero.

Nevertheless its original self-varentropy is
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{p^{(m)}}[\log p^{(m)}_{\mathbf X}]
=(\boldsymbol\theta^{(m)})^\top
  \operatorname{Cov}_{p^{(m)}}(\mathbf X)\boldsymbol\theta^{(m)}
=\frac{m^2}{4}\left(\log\frac53\right)^2
  \frac{2\,15^{m/2}}{2\,15^{m/2}+3^m}.
\]
Consequently this variance divided by \(n=m+1\) tends to infinity. There is no finite absolute constant \(A\) bounding it by \(An\) on the class in the subgoal.

The original atomic terms also vanish at the dimensional normalizations. With \(p^{(m)}_{\max}=\max_{\mathbf x\in D^{(m)}}p^{(m)}_{\mathbf x}\) and \(\rho_m=2^{m+1}p^{(m)}_{\max}\), one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_m&=\frac{(2/3)^m}{1+\tfrac12(3/5)^{m/2}}<(2/3)^m\longrightarrow0,\\
4^{m+1}\sum_{\mathbf x\in D^{(m)}}(p^{(m)}_{\mathbf x})^3
&\le\rho_m^2\longrightarrow0,\\
8^{m+1}\sum_{\mathbf x\in D^{(m)}}(p^{(m)}_{\mathbf x})^4
&\le\rho_m^3\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are original atomic sums, not actual depth moments \(\mathcal M_2\) or \(\mathcal M_3\).

For the exact canonical normalization map, substitute \(A=D^{(m)}\), \(p=p^{(m)}\), and \(\mathbf j=\mathbf j^{(m)}\) into the entropy-row definitions of `bf1ff94487296374` and `3e1cc0fa666b159b`. Their rows satisfy \(r_{D^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}=\nu_{p^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}=p^{(m)}\), and \(\mathsf C_{p^{(m)}}(\mathbf j^{(m)})=1\). Thus the canonical likelihood variance is
\[
V_{p^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}
=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{p^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}}
  \left[\log\frac{\nu_{p^{(m)},\mathbf j^{(m)}}(\mathbf X)}
                    {p^{(m)}_{\mathbf X}}\right]=0.
\]
This zero likelihood variance is not the self-varentropy displayed above. The latter uses the original probability root \(p^{(m)}\), not the capacity weights \(\omega_{p,\mathbf j}\) of `3e1cc0fa666b159b`, and is not an alias of a canonical mutual information \(I\). No value or bound for \(I\) is used or asserted here.
